This novel's protagonist mocks a portrait of Goethe at an old professor's home. His titular description is explained in a treatise bought from a hawker, and after discussing his life with a girl at the Black Eagle Tavern, the title character dances with Maria and eventually sleeps with her. Another character in this work is Pablo the saxophonist, who takes the protagonist to the Magic Theater which includes a room in which Pablo and Hermine lie naked together, prompting the protagonist to stab Hermine. Name this Herman Hesse work about Harry Haller, who identifies with a certain animal.

While disguised, this character claims to be named Sarah Williams and Mary Williams to the same person. This character intervenes in the feud between the Grangerfords and the Shepherdsons and also tries to thwart a plot to con the family of Peter Wilks out of that man's estate. He originally lives in a house shared by Miss Watson and Widow Douglas, but is kidnapped by Pap, his drunkard father, and ends up fleeing with a runaway slave named Jim on a raft down the river. Identify this title character of a Mark Twain novel who is friends with Tom Sawyer.

In one play by this author, Sir Lucius O'Trigger and Bob Acres are the two other suitors of the main character's love interest, whom he woos by disguising himself as Ensign Beverly. In that work, Lydia wants to sleep with a poor soldier to irk her mother. Another comedy by this author sees Sir Oliver return from India disguised as Mr. Premium and as Stanley. In that play, Lady Sneerwell intervenes in the lives of the Surface brothers Charles and Joseph. Name this Irish playwright who wrote The School for Scandal and created Captain Jack Absolute and Mrs. Malaprop in The Rivals.

The monastery of Arkadi is defended against the Turks in one novel by this author sometimes titled after its protagonist Captain Michalis, while another work of this author concerns the staging of a passion play featuring Manolios. This author of Freedom or Death and The Greek Passion created a character who declines Judas's invitation to participate in a rebellion in support of the Zealot and loves Mary Magdalene. In another novel by this author, the title character marries Madame Hortense while working at a lignite mine. Identify this Cretan author of The Last Temptation of Christ who also wrote Zorba the Greek.

One poem from this nation features the landscape on the way to Mount Kailasa, which is the subject of an exiled man's description to the title figure. That work's author wrote a play about the prevention of marriage between the title character and the king by the loss of a signet ring. One poetry collection from this nation begins with "thou hast made me endless, such is thy pleasure," and was prefaced by W. B. Yeats, while this nation's national anthem is Jana Gana Mana. Name this country that produced the play The Recognition of Shakuntala and the collection Gitanjali, home to the authors Kalidasa and Rabindranath Tagore.

One of this author's novels sees the wealthy Dmitri Nekhludoff seek redemption for an affair with Maslova, who suffers in a Siberian labor camp. In addition to writing Resurrection, this author created Gerasim, the servant of a man who dies after falling from a ladder while hanging drapes. In another work, Prince Andrey and Nikolay Rostov defend Moscow against Napoleon, and one of this man's title characters has an affair with Vronsky before throwing herself before a train. Identify this Russian novelist of The Death of Ivan Ilyich, War and Peace, and Anna Karenina.

In one novel set in this city, Sally's disloyalty gets Esperanza Cordero raped at a carnival. It is in this city that the brother of Simon works for the financier Einhorn in a novel by Saul Bellow, and in another novel Charles Drouet meets Caroline Meeber on a train trip to this city. The wealthy Dalton family employs Bigger Thomas, who is captured after a chase scene over this city's rooftops. The House on Mango Street, Sister Carrie, The Adventures of Augie March, and Native Son are all set in, what city celebrated as "hog butcher for the world" by Carl Sandburg?

This character is told that a glass of Constantia wine is perfect for treating old colicky gout and promptly drinks one intended for her sister, which had been offered by Mrs. Jennings. One character tells her that his former fiancée has married his brother Robert. That fiancée was one of Lady Middleton's cousins named Lucy Steele. Subsequently, Edward Ferrars asks this character to marry him. Name this protagonist of Jane Austen's Sense and Sensibility, the sister of Marianne Dashwood.

The protagonist of this novel blackmails the chemist Alan Campbell to hide a body, and he believes himself reformed after beginning a relationship with the vicar's daughter Hetty Merton. An untitled "poisonous French novel" influences the protagonist following the death of his former lover, who swallowed prussic acid after the protagonist left her because she had lost her acting abilities. Lord Henry Wotton's hedonism tempts the protagonist to enchant the title object, created by Basil Hallward, allowing him to remain forever young. Name this novel by Oscar Wilde about a painting that depicts the title character's aging.

One character in this work has a retinue that includes Fagotto and Abadonna. This work opens with two men in a park meeting a stranger who predicts that one of them will die in a car accident later that day. One of this novel's title characters attends a ball in the dead Berlioz's apartment and submits to the stranger, who has a black cat named Behemoth and is revealed to be Woland, the Devil. Another title character of this work commits himself to an insane asylum after abandoning his novel about Yeshua Ha-Nozri and Pontius Pilate. Identify this novel about two lovers in Soviet Russia, written by Mikhail Bulgakov.

In one work attributed to this author, a gnat is killed after waking a sleeping shepherd but saving him from a snakebite. One poem by this author in four sections ends with a discussion on bee-keeping, and this author wrote a collection of ten pastoral poems in the style of Theocritus. This author of the Georgics and Eclogues is more famous for a work concerning a war over the hand of Lavinia between the title character and Turnus. That work earlier features the romance between Dido and the title Trojan prince. Identify this Roman poet who was commissioned by Augustus to write his epic poem, The Aeneid.

This poet asserted "May this right hand be wither'd for ever/ Ere it string our high harp for the foe" in his poem "By the Rivers of Babylon we Sat Down and Wept." That poet wrote of how "the idols are broke in the temple of Baal" and recounted how "the sheen of their spears was like stars on the sea" in a poem beginning "The Assyrian came down like the wolf on the fold," titled "The Destruction of Sennacherib." This poet of "She Walks in Beauty" and Childe Harold's Pilgrimage wrote an unfinished seventeen-canto epic poem about a man who is seduced by a long succession of women. Name this author of Don Juan.

One work by this author follows Jourdain's foolish attempts to enter the nobility and ends with his daughter's marriage to a man pretending to be a Turkish prince. Another work by this author shows Arnolphe's failure to raise Agnes to be a faithful wife, while this author's last play sees Angelique remain faithful to her hypochondriacal father Argan. In another play by this author of The Bourgeois Gentleman and The School for Wives, Orgon is nearly tricked out of ownership of his home by the title hypocrite. Name this French playwright of The Imaginary Invalid and Tartuffe.

In one story from this work, a man kills a tiger after consuming lots of alcohol and later kills his sister-in-law to avenge the death of his brother. Another character in this work was framed by a government official lusting after his wife. The central characters of this work are comprised of two groups, one being the Thirty-Six Stars of Heavenly Spirits. Mt. Liang is a central gathering point in this novel, in which both Lin and Wu follow Song Jiang, the leader of the titular group. Name this work by Shi Na'ian about 108 criminals during the Song dynasty.

This man wrote "if the quote state unquote says ‘kill'killing is an act of christian love" in a work ending with the line "Ain't freedom grand." He also wrote of a man who mentions some things he won't eat as well and that he won't kiss your flag when he is abused for being a "conscientious object-or" since his "warmest heart recoiled at war." This man also wrote about a place "with up so floating many bells down." identify this author of "I sing of Olaf glad and big" and "anyone lived in a pretty how town," a poet who was fond of lowercase letters.

The sequel to this novel features a character who gets a job with Mr. Green at the Public Service Commission. The protagonist of this work is exiled seven years after the gun he is holding discharges and kills another man. Earlier, Chielo carries Ezinma off to perform a religious ritual in the middle of the night, and the protagonist breaks the Week of Peace by beating his third wife. Nwoye's decision to convert to Christianity angers the protagonist of this work, who takes part in the killing of Ikemefuna and eventually hangs himself after killing an Umuofian messenger. Name this work about Okonkwo's struggle with colonialism, written by Chinua Achebe.

This character is described as halfway through the course of his wife, and this character encounters a lion, leopard, and wolf in succession. At one point, this character rides the monster Geryon to see Mahomet among the victims of their fraudulent actions. This character is first seen contemplating death in a forest and witnesses the heads of Judas, Brutus, and Cassius being devoured by Lucifer before he is led through God's kingdom by his love Beatrice. Name this Italian poet who is led by Virgil through Hell and Purgatory and by Beatrice through Paradise, the protagonist of his own work The Divine Comedy.

This character once fell into a canal chasing a small bird and was later arrested by Mr. Fellamar after stabbing Mr. Fitzpatrick. This character saves another Mr. Nightingale from being throttled at the hands of his footman, and later Mr. Nightingale marries Nancy. This character's schoolmaster, who lives with the philosopher Mr. Square, is the harsh Mr. Thwackum. He kills a partridge for Black George and falls in love with Sophia Western, having earlier been taken in by Squire Allworthy. Identify this character, the title foundling in a novel by Henry Fielding.

One character in this play discusses the expression "all hawk and no spit," and obnoxious children in this play are called "no-neck monsters." Minor characters in this work include Reverend Tooker and Doc Baugh from the Ochsner Clinic, and another character in this play is bothered by the suicide of his friend Skipper. One character worries that Gooper and Mae will get the inheritance from the cotton planter Big Daddy, and whose birthday this play is set. Identify this play set in the Mississippi Delta centering on Brick and Maggie Pollitt, a work of Tennessee Williams.
Cat on a Hot Tin Roof

One figure in this work suggests that he be given free meals in the Prytaneum. One group in this work claims to represent the craftsmen and politicians, the professional rhetoricians, and the poets; those men are Lycon, Anytus, and Meletus. The central figure of this work claims to be a stinging gadfly to the horse of the state, and argues that since he has never acted as a teacher, he cannot be held responsible for any corruption. The second part sees the central figure condemned to drink hemlock and die. Name this Platonic dialogue in which Socrates delivers the title address, responding to charges of atheism and corrupting the youth.

This play opens with various priests and suppliants gathered and holding "branches of olive filleted with wool."At one point in this play a shepherd reveals that he had found another character in this play on Mount Cithaeron before taking him to Polybus and Merope of Corinth. Later in this play, the protagonist uses the pins that had held together his wife's dress to gouge out his own eyes, upon realizing he had killed his father Laius and married his mother Jocasta. Name this play about the titular king of Thebes, which appears in a trilogy by Sophocles.

This author's lesser-known works include one about Polly Milton's attempt to fit in with the classy family of her friend Fanny Shaw and another satirizing her life in the experimental Fruitlands community. In addition to An Old Fashioned Girl and "Transcendental Wild Oats," this author published a set of four stories written during her time as a Civil War nurse entitled Hospital Sketches. This author is best known for a series of works in which Professor Bhaer and his wife run the Plumfield School and Beth, daughter of Marmee and sister of Meg and Amy, dies of scarlet fever. Name this creator of March family, the author of Jo's Boys, Little Men, and Little Women.

One character in this novel bankrupts her servant Briggs and landlord Raggles, has an affair with the Marquess of Steyne, and plays Clytemnestra in a game of charades. Earlier, that character had thrown a copy of Samuel Johnson's Dictionary out of a coach window. One character in this novel proposes to the woman he'd employed as a governess only to discover that she had already married his son Rawdon Crawley. This novel takes its title from the location where Faithful is executed in Pilgrim's Progress. Name this novel subtitled "A Novel without a Hero" about Amelia Sedley and Becky Sharp, written by William Makepeace Thackeray.
Vanity Fair: A Novel without a Hero

After learning that the lights cannot be put out in this play, one character remarks, "so you have to live with your eyes open." A woman mistakes that character for her torturer when they meet in a room with a bronze statue and Second Empire furniture. When given the option to leave, the characters decline for fear of the unknown, and one discussion in this play about each person's transgressions reveals that Estelle had murdered her illegitimate child. Name this play in which Garcin declares that "Hell is other people," written by Jean-Paul Sartre.

The development of a nuclear bomb under the control of the Patron is opposed by Mori and his father in one novel by this author, while another work follows a group of boys who are barricaded inside a plague-ridden village. This author of The Pinch Runner Memorandum wrote of Bird's reluctance to care for his mentally handicapped son in one work, while another work features the selling of a kura-yashiki to the Emperor, a wealthy Korean man living in Mitsusaburo and Takashi's village. Identify this Japanese author of A Personal Matter and The Silent Cry.

Two characters in this novel become friends upon learning they had both been stealing Voltaire works from a nobleman's library. Earlier, the protagonist had declined Fouque's invitation to join the lumber business and had served in a seminary at Besancon where he befriended Abbe Pirard. Eventually, this work's protagonist shoots Madame de Renal for revealing their previous affair and ruining his chances with Mathilde de La Mole. Name this work about Julien Sorel, whose titular colors refer to the army and the clergy in French society, written by Stendhal.

One play by this author sees a man trip over a drum after another breaks his glasses during a game of blind man's bluff. This author wrote a play chronicling "seven years of afternoons" during which Emma, Robert's wife, slept with Jerry. That play is told in reverse chronology and is titled Betrayal. This author also wrote of an old tramp named Davies filling the title role in The Caretaker, and another play by this author sees two characters receiving orders for food until one, Ben, realizes that he has been hired to kill the other, Gus. Name this British author of The Dumb Waiter.

In one novel by this author, Athena College professor Coleman Silk loses his job after he is accused of racism. That novel forms part of a trilogy along with I Married a Communist and is titled The Human Stain. In another of this author's novels, the relationship between working class Neil Krugman and affluent Brenda Patimkin falls apart, while this man also wrote about of a character who explains to Dr. Spielvogel his relationships with "The Pilgrim," "The Pumpkin," and "The Monkey." The creator of Nathan Zuckerman, identify this American author of Goodbye, Columbus and Portnoy's Complaint.

A library in this short story contained such books as Pomponius Mela's De Situ Orbis and Tommaso Campanella's The City of the Sun, and one character was described by "a suspiciously lingering smile upon the lip." The narrator of this story reads a tale written by Sir Launcelot Canning about a knight Ethelred called the Mad Trist. In this story, Madeline was entombed in a vault, but during a storm she cries out and Roderick fell to the floor as a corpse. Identify this story which ends when the title abode breaks and two and sinks into a lake, written by Edgar Allan Poe.
The Fall of the House of Usher

This author wrote a novel about an Italian woman who befriends Savanorola and marries Tito, while in another work Harold Transome loses a Parliamentary election and the title character marries Esther Lyon. This author described Mirah Lapidoth's search for her family and Gwendolen Harleth's financial woes in another novel. However, this author of Romola, Felix Holt the Radical, and Daniel Deronda and is most famous for a work in which Edward Casaubon's will prevents his widow from marrying Will Ladislaw. Name this English creator of Dorothea Brooke in Middlemarch.

In one novel by this author, Said experiences betrayal from his wife and Rauf, his mentor in crime. Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad are among the title group in another work by this man, which recreates the origins of the Abrahamic religions. This author of The Thief and the Dogs wrote about Fahmy, an activist against British control, and his brother Yasin Abd al-Jawad, who like his father takes part in immoral pleasures. Name this author of Children of Gebelawi, an Egyptian writer whose Palace Walk, Palace of Desire, and Sugar Street form his Cairo Trilogy.

Failure from Holofernes and Joberlin Bride lead this character's father to send him to study with Ponocrates. Born from his mother's left ear, this character needed milk from nearly eighteen thousand cows and once tied Notre Dame's bells around his horse's neck. After helping Grangosier defeat the army of Lerne, this character builds the Abbey of Theleme for Friar John, and later his son befriends Panurge. Name this patron saint of revelry, a giant created by Francois Rabelais and the father of Pantagruel.

In this novel, the protagonist's fiance vacations in St. Augustine with her parents, and the protagonist falls in love with another woman at the engagement party. Mrs. Mingott, the de facto head of the family, suffers a stroke after another character sees his firm collapse. That man, Julius Beaufort, is also interested in a woman married to a Polish count. This novel ends when the protagonist's son Dallas takes him to Paris to see his former lover, and although the protagonist is free to court her because May Welland had already died, he chooses not to meet Ellen Olenska. Name this novel about Newland Archer, set in New York and written by Edith Wharton.

The protagonist of this novel buys Hortense a fur coat instead of spending the money to support his pregnant sister, and soon afterward he is involved in a hit and run car accident. After meeting his uncle Samuel in Chicago while working for the Union League Club, he travels to Lycurgus in New York where he is scorned by his cousin Gilbert. At the end of this novel, the protagonist is electrocuted for his crime, which was motivated by his desire to marry Sondra Finchley and move himself into upper class society, as well as the need to hide Roberta Alden's pregnancy. Name this Theodore Dreiser novel in which Clyde Griffiths murders his lover on a lake.

One author from this country wrote a novella in which Dalmacio Ombrellieri leads The Fugitive to a two-sunned island home to Faustine and The Invention of Morel. That author, Bioy Casares, shows an encyclopedia article to another author from this country in the short story "Tlon, Uqbar, Orbus Tertius.". That author wrote a short story in which Richard Madden pursues the German spy Yu Tsun and included in his collection Ficciones, "The Garden of Forking Paths." name this country home to Jorge Luis Borges, the setting of Manuel Puig's The Buenos Aires Affair.

One of this author's novels begins after a man who was seduced by a servant girl leaves his umbrella below-decks on a ship. In another of this author's works, the protagonist meets the painter Titorelli and the lawyer Herr Huld. Karl Rossman befriends a stoker in this author's Amerika, and Josef K. Dies "like a dog" in another work. This author of The Trial is most famous for a novella whose protagonist has apples thrown at him by his father and dreams of sending his sister Grete to play violin at the conservatory. Name this author who wrote of Gregor Samsa's transformation into a bug in The Metamorphosis.

This work's antagonist is shot after saving a drowning girl, and before that learns of the love between Felix and the Turkish Safie. Alphonse, the father of the protagonist, dies soon after his son's wedding night, and Justine Moritz is framed for the murder of William. The frame story of this novel is told in a series of letters written to Margaret Saville by her brother, ship captain Robert Walton. The protagonist of this novel is friends with Henry Clerval, and marries Elizabeth Lavenza. Identify this Mary Shelley novel in which Victor, the title scientist, creates a monster in the lab.

In one of this author's novels, Lady Russell convinces the protagonist to break off her engagement with Frederick Wentworth. In another, Mr. Yates encourages a production of the play Lovers' Vows while Thomas Bertram is away. In addition to writing about Anne Elliot in Persuasion, this author wrote a book in which John Willoughby hits on a woman who sprains her ankle in the rain, Marianne Dashwood. This author's most famous work sees clergyman William Collins marry Charlotte Lucas, and Georgiana helps her brother Fitzwilliam Darcy end up with Elizabeth Bennet. Name this author of Sense and Sensibility and Pride and Prejudice.

In one of this author's works, a doctor delivers a baby by C-section with a knife while its Native American father slits his own throat. That story features a character who more famously warns that Max and Al will kill Ole Anderson. In addition to writing "Indian Camp" and "The Killers" about Nick Adams, this author wrote a novel whose main character walks back to his hotel in the rain after discovering that his child was stillborn and his wife Catherine Barkley is dead. Name this author who wrote about Frederic Henry in A Farewell to Arms.

One of this author's short stories begins by describing a "certain official" who "serves in a certain department," and another contrasts the lives of Lieutenant Pirogov and Piskaryov, who both travel along the title street. In another of his works, Poprischin believes himself heir to the throne of Spain. This author of "Diary of a Madman" and "Nevsky Prospekt" wrote an unfinished novel whose title objects are bought from characters like Plyushkin and Sobakevich by the crafty Chichikov. Identify this author who wrote of Akaky Akakievich losing the title garment in "The Overcoat," and also wrote Dead Souls.

The Arawaks exchanged this commodity for tokens that prevented their hands from being cut off. While Don Pedro II was in Europe, an 1888 law named after this substance abolished slavery in Brazil. Slaves gathered this substance in the Kerma region of Nubia during the Egyptian New Kingdom. Francisco Coronado searched for Cibola and the Seven Cities of this substance. Mansa Musa depleted the price of this commodity in Egypt by giving it out during his hajj, of which the Mali empire had gained so much by trading salt for it. Identify this precious metal, the the discovery of which prompted an 1849 "rush" in California.

In one of this author's novels, people drown while trying to cross the Arabian Sea by foot. In another, Boonyi betrays the title character by having an affair with Max Ophuls. This author of Shalimar the Clown wrote a novel which sees Joseph D'Costa's lover Mary Pereira play a trick on Mumtaz, the daughter of Aadam Aziz. In this man's most famous novel, mountaineer Allie Cone is killed by Gibreel Farishta, who, like Saladin Chamcha, had survived a plane explosion over the English Channel. Identify this author who wrote about Saleem Sinai in Midnight's Children and earned a fatwa for The Satanic Verses.

One work inspired by this poem mentions the "always coming on / The always rising of the night." This poem's narrator would not mind two hundred years "to adore each breast" and thirty thousand years "for the rest," before noting that "the grave's a fine and private place." This poem's speaker's "vegetable love" would "grow vaster than Empires" if it weren't for the coming "deserts of vast eternity" and "time's winged chariot hurrying near." identify this metaphysical poem beginning "Had we but world enough, and time," in which Andrew Marvell tries to get a reluctant woman to sleep with him.

This novel's narrator describes another's parking of cars in an incredibly long sentence, and later "realized what a rat" that character was after being abandoned with dysentery in Mexico. That "Holy goof" impregnates Inez despite his involvement with Marylou and Camille, and this novel's narrator is friends with Old Bull Lee and Remi Boncoeur. This novel's manuscript was written on a giant scroll, and its character Carlo Marx represents Allen Ginsberg. Name this Beat novel about the cross-country travels of Dean Moriarty and Sal Paradise written by Jack Kerouac.
